text: Friday, the day before the raid, brings a private rehearsal: a D-grade gate, a ruined aqueduct, and a basalt-plated boar the size of a truck.
It slams into Borro's shield and shoves him back through the water.
The aqueduct cracks under his heels, and the gorge is a long way down. Both summons are already on the clock.
Nib leaps onto its back, and once again his knives skid off in sparks.
The boar bucks him into the water and wheels away for another run.
Back by the gate, both impacts land in Jaeha at once.
Bomi is suffering. Her drone is switched off by contract, and Choi, with his coffee and stopwatch, has no sympathy.
Jaeha wipes his nose. Whatever goes wrong today, nobody will ever see it.
Between them, they have the whole problem. Nib's knives bounce off all that paving, and Borro's shield only buys time.
Jaeha writes it down the way he writes everything: one has speed, one has weight, and neither has both.
Far down the channel, the boar lowers its head.
So they run the same play again, one summon holding and one hunting for a seam.
The next charge buckles Borro's shield.
And this time, Jaeha feels exactly where the force goes: in through Borro's link, down through his body, and out into the stone.
Carry has always meant taking the hit and keeping it. But it doesn't stay. It passes through.
And anything that passes through him can be aimed. Somewhere more useful than the floor.
Yerin can't believe it: he walks right out onto the cracking channel, notebook shut, with a small fierce smile.
Crouched behind the buckled shield, he pitches it: Borro's hit, through him, into Nib's knife. Nib has one fair objection.
Jaeha grins, a little mad. He has been a professional tester for four years.
The boar charges, and Nib crouches to spring.
Impact. A ragged pulse tears out of Jaeha toward Nib, but Nib jumped too early, and it scatters into sparks.
Nib's knife glances off, and a tusk rips across Borro's arm.
The same cut opens on Jaeha's forearm, his nose bleeds, and his ears ring. Failing hurts too.
Yerin runs out across the cracking stone to him, and she has no patience for Choi's warning.
Bleeding, and glared at by his healer, Jaeha laughs anyway. The timing was off. The idea wasn't.
Then both clocks run out together. For one minute, neither summon can fight.
Jaeha uses the minute. Every boss has a tell, and this one's head gives the count.
The new plan puts all three of them in one line: the shield takes the hit, Jaeha is the wire, and Nib is the point.
With fresh clocks, Nib balances on the rim of Borro's shield like a cat on a fence, and Jaeha lays a hand on the shell.
Borro offers some dry encouragement from below. Nib's answer is even drier.
The boar charges, and its head starts to drop.
Each stride drops the head a little lower, and Jaeha counts them under his breath.
Impact. The force runs from the shield through Borro, through Jaeha, and up the link into Nib, who drops onto the boar's skull with it blazing down his arms.
The road it was wearing splits open like broken paving.
The boar collapses into the water, its plates sliding off.
It dissolves into ash. Behind Borro, Jaeha has sunk to his knees.
His raised hand trembles violently, a white-gold glow fading from the skin.
Blood trickles from one ear. He's smiling anyway.
The system names it: Pass. He can hand one summon's force to the other, but every hand-off leaks thirty percent.
And the fine print, in red, confirms what his ear already knows: the force has to go through him to get anywhere.
Nib turns a knife over in his hand, and the corner of his mouth almost moves. For Nib, that's a standing ovation.
Borro, peering at the dent in his shield, has a counter-proposal.
Nib with a pot-lid shield, sweating. Borro with a cup of tea, smug.
Bomi is close to tears over the shot she missed. Choi, eyeing his stopwatch, is glad nobody got it.
Yerin hauls him up, listing his injuries. Jaeha only hears the good part.
A violet core rises from the water.
Three and a half million won, and again, one button. Nib looks away down the channel.
His list has four entries now, each with the same mark, and one question he can't answer yet.
A boss he's never fought before, and that's the last ten percent: Route Alignment is full.
Which means the Call is open again. One press, and a third summon could answer before the raid.
Yerin is all for it. Borro, ever the host, starts thinking about sleeping arrangements.
But Jaeha thinks like the opposition. Sora's compass hunts summons, and every plan Mok has made counts exactly two.
His finger hovers over the button, then curls back.
He sweeps the window down to a point of light. A third summon nobody has counted is worth more inside the gate.
Nib gives one small nod, soldier to soldier. He has always believed in a spare blade.
Choi hands him a coffee and watches it shake in his hands. Jaeha has an answer for that too.
That's what he'll be holding: at the edge of his vision, one tiny mark stays pinned. A Call, kept in reserve.
They walk out into the noon light, Nib and Borro back in their husk faces.
By this time tomorrow, Mok will have exactly what he asked for, and he won't like it.
